macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Fed holds rates steady with two dissenting votes
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest-rate target at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 vote. Two officials favored a quarter-point increase, while Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments were viewed as relatively dovish, leaving markets uncertain about a possible December move.

items.title: U.S. stocks close modestly higher after Fed decision
items.summary: The Dow rose 0.19% to 52,479.62, the S&P 500 gained 0.28% to 7,743.98, and the Nasdaq advanced 0.27% to 26,549.85. Trading remained restrained as investors assessed the Fed decision and awaited major technology earnings.

items.title: Oil prices rise on renewed supply-disruption concerns
items.summary: Crude prices moved higher amid concerns about potential supply disruptions after an attack on a Saudi refinery attributed to Iran-backed Houthis. Higher oil prices added to inflation concerns facing markets.

items.title: Microsoft beats cloud-revenue expectations
items.summary: Microsoft shares rose in extended trading after the company reported quarterly revenue above Wall Street expectations, supported by stronger cloud performance.

items.title: Alphabet advertising revenue misses expectations
items.summary: Alphabet shares fell after hours after the Google parent reported advertising revenue below analyst expectations, putting pressure on the company’s stock despite broader market gains.

items.title: Vertiv raises outlook after strong quarterly results
items.summary: Vertiv jumped roughly 16.6% after reporting third-quarter sales growth of 61% and raising its full-year sales forecast by $650 million, benefiting from demand for data-center power and cooling infrastructure.

items.title: Wendy’s receives takeover proposal
items.summary: Wendy’s shares rose about 15% after the company confirmed it had received a non-binding cash proposal of $7.35 per share from Trian Partners and affiliates led by Nelson Peltz.

items.title: SK hynix reports record results and signals tight memory supply
items.summary: South Korea’s SK hynix reported a sharp increase in quarterly profit and said memory demand could outpace supply through 2030, lifting semiconductor and artificial-intelligence-related shares globally.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies edge higher after Fed holds rates
items.summary: Bitcoin rose 0.3% to about $80,834 over 24 hours, while Ethereum gained 0.2% and Solana and Dogecoin rose 0.6%; XRP fell 0.7%. Total crypto market capitalization increased 0.7% to $2.82 trillion, with roughly $260 million in positions liquidated.[5]

items.title: U.S. Federal Reserve keeps interest rates unchanged
items.summary: The Fed maintained its target range at 3.75%–4%, with two officials dissenting in favor of a quarter-point increase. Bitcoin traded above $80,000 as markets assessed the decision.[5]

items.title: DTCC launches tokenization service for real-world assets
items.summary: The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation launched a service allowing tokenized representations of DTCC-custodied real-world assets, marking a major expansion of blockchain infrastructure in U.S. securities markets.[9]

items.title: Taiwan passes virtual-asset regulation
items.summary: Taiwan’s legislature passed the Virtual Asset Service Act, requiring virtual-asset service providers and stablecoin issuers to obtain approval from the Financial Supervisory Commission. Violations can carry prison terms of up to 10 years.[4]

items.title: Moody’s assigns investment-grade ratings to Ripple’s RLUSD
items.summary: Moody’s rated Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin A2 for long-term deposits and P-1 for short-term obligations, placing the ratings in the investment-grade category.[8]

items.title: Mirae Asset completes tokenized financing note on Solana
items.summary: Mirae Asset Securities Hong Kong completed issuance of a U.S.-dollar-denominated, six-month floating-rate tokenized financing note on Solana for qualified institutional investors.[1]

items.title: Crypto.com launches regulated U.S. perpetual futures
items.summary: Crypto.com and OG.com launched regulated cryptocurrency perpetual futures for eligible U.S. traders, offering leverage of up to five times and bringing the product into the regulated U.S. derivatives market.[7]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model focused on cybersecurity, complex programming, and long-horizon tasks. Initial access is limited to selected cyber defenders and trusted partners, with broader availability planned later.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly plans to use Google TPU chips
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly intends to purchase Google’s custom TPU accelerators as it expands AI infrastructure and seeks alternatives to relying exclusively on Nvidia GPUs. The company is also hiring engineers to optimize frontier models for TPUs.

items.title: Google DeepMind previews Genie 4 world model
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4, a model that generates interactive, real-time simulated environments with visuals, sound, and dialogue. The research preview is available to selected testers in areas including gaming, education, journalism, and engineering.

items.title: OpenAI and ServiceNow expand partnership
items.summary: OpenAI and ServiceNow are expanding their partnership to integrate OpenAI models and agents into ServiceNow products while bringing ServiceNow workflows and business context into ChatGPT and Codex.

items.title: AMD invests $1 billion in Meta
items.summary: AMD announced a $1 billion investment in Meta and said its first Helios AI rack systems are operating at Meta. The deal follows a separate $3 billion Nvidia investment in Meta.

items.title: New York restricts unsafe chatbot behavior involving minors
items.summary: New York enacted restrictions on certain AI companion behaviors involving children. Violations of the new requirements can result in fines, extending state-level regulation of AI systems used by minors.

items.title: Oracle to offer Google TPUs in its cloud
items.summary: Oracle plans to rent Google Tensor Processing Units through its cloud beginning in 2027, potentially making it the first major cloud provider outside Google to offer the accelerators.

items.title: Google adds third-party agents to Android Studio
items.summary: Google introduced a Bring Your Own Agent feature for Android Studio, enabling developers to connect more than 40 external coding agents, including Claude Agent and OpenAI Codex.

items.title: Anthropic files for a potentially record-setting IPO
items.summary: Anthropic filed paperwork for a public offering that could become one of the largest technology IPOs. The filing also details potential risks from advanced AI, including cyberattacks and dangerous misinformation.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Epic confirms AI-assisted development for Fortnite and Unreal Engine 6
items.summary: Epic Games executive vice president Marcus Wassmer said the company is using AI-assisted or “vibe-coding” workflows for Fortnite, UEFN, Unreal Engine and Unreal Engine 6. He said engineers guide AI tools rather than writing most of the code manually.[1][2]

items.title: Nintendo showcases 23 indie games for Switch and Switch 2
items.summary: Nintendo’s latest Indie World presentation featured 23 games, including new announcements, updates and release information for titles coming to Switch and Switch 2.[9]

items.title: Nintendo highlights upcoming indie releases
items.summary: Nintendo’s showcase included a range of independent games, from retro-styled adventures to a cooperative raccoon simulator, and revealed a release date for My Arms Are Longer Now.[4]

items.title: Wardogs tops September PC revenue rankings
items.summary: Bulkhead’s Early Access shooter Wardogs ranked first in Newzoo’s September PC revenue chart, ahead of EA Sports FC 27. Marvel’s Wolverine ranked fourth on console, while several other new releases entered the monthly rankings.[7]

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple unveils first touchscreen MacBooks
items.summary: Apple introduced its first touchscreen MacBook models as part of a broader product launch ahead of the holiday shopping season. The move reverses the company’s longstanding resistance to touchscreen laptops.
